scope: Complete HBQ moduleNavArea helper and CBE native/optional ZEN task registration chain
findings: HBQ registers once on every machine, reading Eden objectArea half-width/length, arrow direction and initial centre. It stores a flattened centre and static axis in a local list. Activated is parsed but not used.

The reviewed driveAssist navigation consumer uses the first three row fields; module half-width is not a demonstrated runtime width constraint there. Do not claim active width handling merely from its registration.

CBE provides explicit native Zeus/optional labelled ZEN create/update/remove behaviour tasks with authenticated server dispatch, live area transforms, definition revisions, passive public snapshot and current-owner execution. CBA configuration remains separate.

Trusted scheduled server calls could interleave registry/request read-modify-write despite usual remoteExecCall delivery being unscheduled. Serializing only the remote entry assumption did not cover those callers.
implementation: Registration now serializes bounded snapshot validation/revision/area update/publication.
Dispatch now serializes request sequence/budget validation, explicit area creation/update/removal and registration/answer publication.
No additional movement authority, hidden nearest-object selection, global loop, world query or copied upstream code.
remaining: CBE native frontend currently requires interface/local logic and is curator-facing; HBQ Eden objectArea placement is not implemented as equivalent CBE Eden task authoring.
CBE geometry refuses wet unsupported/terrain-water paths. HBQ shallow-ford intent is not implemented; requires a separate explicit depth/vehicle suitability and physical support policy.
Actual multiplayer curator transforms/deletion, concurrent script calls, repeated task use and JIP require physical validation.
Whole-HBQ startup, controllers, queue/native reverse and measured runtime performance remain incomplete.
